name: Gaussian Shuffle Split
definition: A training-free local Gaussian densification strategy that replaces one large Gaussian primitive with six smaller sub-Gaussians to facilitate fine-grained detail representation in high-resolution scenes.
summary: Gaussian Shuffle Split is a training-free local densification strategy that replaces large Gaussians with six sub-Gaussians based on opacity thresholds, avoiding gradient-based splitting or octree structures.
